origin: Named after a Japanese bento box divided into compartments: cells of different sizes packed into one tray. It became widely known through Apple's product pages.
whenToUse: A set of features on a product page.
You gather information of different importance on one screen.
whenNotToUse: All items are equally important (use a responsive grid).
Explanations whose reading order matters (use a list).
Cells get too small on narrow screens (stack them in one column).
accessibility: Keep the DOM in reading order and change cell sizes only with grid spans.
Put the most important content in the largest cell, which is also the first.
Keep the contrast between text and background inside tiles.
On narrow screens, stack in one column so it stays readable when zoomed.
